issues.legal_issue: A High Court exercising general civil revisional jurisdiction cannot correct a subordinate court’s error in construing a decree when that error has no relation to the subordinate court’s jurisdiction.
material_facts: In debt-adjustment proceedings, the District Court decided that a prior decree had extinguished the applicants’ right to redeem the mortgaged property.
The High Court, exercising general revisional jurisdiction, construed the decree differently and set aside the District Court’s decision.
The challenged construction concerned whether the debt and right of redemption remained subsisting, a matter the courts administering the debt-adjustment proceedings were authorized to determine.
The error alleged against the District Court’s construction did not concern its assumption, failure to exercise, or manner of exercising jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: The High Court exceeded its revisional jurisdiction by interfering with the District Court’s construction of the decree; its order was set aside and the District Court’s order restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 115(a), (b) and (c) of the Code of Civil Procedure, revisional intervention is confined to cases where a subordinate court has exercised jurisdiction not vested in it, failed to exercise jurisdiction vested in it, or acted illegally or with material irregularity in exercising jurisdiction. An error of law, including an error in construing a decree or document of title, is not by itself enough if it has no relation to jurisdiction. The Court relied on Manindra Land and Building Corporation Ltd. v. Bhutnath Banerjee, A.I.R. 1964 S.C. 1336, and Vora Abbasbhai Alimahomed v. Haji Gulamnabi Haji Safibhai, A.I.R. 1964 S.C. 1341. It noted that limitation and res judicata may raise jurisdictional questions, but did not treat the construction issue in this case as jurisdictional.

predicates.revision_under_limited_civil_revisional_: A party asks a higher court to review a subordinate court’s decision under a limited general civil revisional power.
predicates.subordinate_court_was_authorized_to_deci: The subordinate court was empowered to determine the substantive dispute before it.
predicates.challenged_error_concerned_construction_: The alleged legal error concerned how the subordinate court interpreted a decree.
predicates.challenged_error_had_no_relation_to_juri: The alleged error did not involve the subordinate court’s assumption, refusal to exercise, or exercise of jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When a subordinate court is authorized to decide a dispute, an error in construing a decree that does not affect its jurisdiction cannot be corrected through limited general civil revision.
